title: Chapter 232: Wednesday
html:
Then again, this is not bad. At least I don’t need to explain myself anymore.

Dragging the unconscious Han Qiuming behind him, Chen Ge left the Haunted House and headed naturally toward the rest tent. “Where are the doctors? This gentleman might need a little help.”

“Chen Ge!” Uncle Xu hurried over, unsurprised by the sight. He had stocked the tent outside Chen Ge’s Haunted House with ample emergency supplies. “The stretcher is over there! Stop dragging him! Lay him down properly. Everyone, make room and give him some air!”

The park doctor, who had been waiting nearby, rushed over to examine Han Qiuming. “He’s physically stable, and there are no visible injuries. He didn’t faint from trauma or illness.” The longer the doctor examined him, the more curious he became. “Extreme and sustained psychological stress likely caused his brain to shut down. It’s the body’s natural defense mechanism. He should regain consciousness on his own soon.”

“Doctor Liu, will he end up with some kind of side effects?” Uncle Xu asked worriedly.

“It’s difficult to say. Cases like this are uncommon.” Doctor Liu lifted Han Qiuming’s eyelids. His gaze was unfocused, his mouth hung open, and his body temperature was low. “What kind of ordeal reduced him to this state?”

The sight frightened the other employees as well. “Boss Chen, Mr. Han ended up like this while visiting your Haunted House. You owe us an explanation.”

“I’m curious too. You all entered together, so why is he the only one who ended up in this condition?” Chen Ge shrugged and led them toward Guo Miao and Ye Xiaoxin. “Don’t worry. Our Haunted House has plenty of experience handling situations like this, and we will provide a satisfactory explanation.”

“Plenty of experience?” The employees followed him in a daze. For some reason, Boss Chen’s reassurance only made them more uneasy. Ye Xiaoxin and Guo Miao sat on opposite sides of the steps, still recovering.

“Boss Guo, Han Qiuming entered with your group. You should know better than anyone what happened to him.” Chen Ge passed the question to Guo Miao.

“I have no idea. We became separated.” The smile on Chen Ge’s face made Guo Miao’s scalp prickle. He complained inwardly, Shouldn’t you be the one who knows why he ended up like this?

“Then let me ask differently. In which corridor did you separate, and what was he doing at the time?” Guo Miao could not understand the purpose of the question. Staring at the unconscious Han Qiuming, he found himself at a loss for words. Han Qiuming had proudly declared that he would wreck Chen Ge’s Haunted House, only to disappear two minutes later.

That was the truth, but it was far too humiliating to admit. If Guo Miao said it in front of their employees and fans, how could he remain in the business? Remembering what Chen Ge had done at Tian Teng Medical School, Guo Miao clutched his chest as a fresh pang shot through it.

“Mr. Han might be a Haunted House designer, but he is not that courageous; he was probably spooked by some prop.” Guo Miao forced a smile to end this topic as soon as possible.

“Boss, doesn’t Mr. Han claim he fears nothing—not even the curses of the dead?” A female employee named Ah Rui tried to continue, but Guo Miao silenced her with a glare.

“We can talk about this when we return.”

He pointed surreptitiously at the gathering fans, hoping that she would take the hint.

They helped one another stand. By the time they looked toward the rest tent, the doctor and park employees were already carrying Han Qiuming away. The crowd parted for the stretcher. Unconscious, he knew nothing of the spectacle, but the sight of him lying there with foam at his lips would remain engraved in everyone’s memory.

“My Haunted House’s scenarios are divided into difficulty levels. The Third Sick Hall is rated three stars and is currently the most frightening. The fact that most of you remained conscious is already impressive.” Chen Ge did not raise his voice, but nearby visitors could hear every word. “Normally, guests experience the scenarios in order. That gradually builds their tolerance and makes the challenge much easier.”

The Tian Teng Medical School employees had become an object lesson, much to their fans’ embarrassment. Some of those fans quietly joined the queue, eager to experience Chen Ge’s Haunted House themselves.

“Several props were damaged, and I’ll need half an hour to repair them. In the meantime, you can visit the Minghun scenario.” Chen Ge returned to the Third Sick Hall, repaired the mannequins, and moved them back to Mu Yang High School. “Stop running around! The doctors and patients can manage the other scenario without you.”

Chen Ge closed the Third Sick Hall’s door. Judging by the day’s events, it would be some time before another visitor challenged the scenario. He returned to work. During the lunch break, Ye Xiaoxin sought him out for an interview, explaining that she wanted to promote the Haunted House. After answering a few simple questions, Chen Ge saw her off and began the afternoon shift. The attraction closed at 6:30 p.m. Once he had cleaned the restroom, he lay alone in the staff break room.

This isn’t a bad life—scaring people and counting money by day, playing with the cat at night.

Chen Ge ordered takeout. Before he could begin eating, a phone call pulled him back to reality. “Captain Yan? You wanted to speak with me?”

“We’ve checked the surveillance around Hai Ming Apartments, and we didn’t find anyone suspicious. I need you to tell me where you got this clue.”

When the monster left Wang Shenglong, he had heard a strange sound in the corridor, like someone walking backward. Suspecting that one of the Third Sick Hall’s patients was responsible, Chen Ge had reported it to Captain Yan.

He told Captain Yan everything honestly. After a long silence, the captain replied, “One of the neighbors mentioned this during another investigation. I hope you’ll stay out of the matter from now on.”

“Okay.”

“I’ve also uncovered something about the Ghost Stories Society.” Captain Yan’s tone grew serious. “They are extremely dangerous and connected to numerous cases.”

“What kind of cases?” Chen Ge was intrigued.

“Don’t ask. I’ll tell you what I’m allowed to disclose. Anything beyond that, you won’t get from me.”

“I understand.” Chen Ge did not mind. After all, he had plenty of secrets of his own.

“For your own safety, I’ll share one detail. Every case connected to the society occurred on a Wednesday. The day appears to hold special significance for them, but we still don’t know why.”

“Wednesday? Meaning I’ll need to be careful on every Wednesday?” Chen Ge looked at his phone; it was a Tuesday.

“Take care of yourself.”

After the call ended, Chen Ge lost his appetite. He removed the flyer from his pocket. He preferred taking the initiative to waiting for danger to arrive.

“What is the purpose of this society?”

When he was thinking, his phone rang again. This time, it was from Inspector Lee.

“Chen Ge, come to the Western Jiujiang police station immediately! We found the killer who drove the girl from Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy to suicide four years ago!”
